correctness.rationale: For fixed c>0 and each m>=2, the atomic Fourier Gram matrix is (1-r)I+r11* with r=c/(m+c), positive eigenvalues 1-r and 1+(m-1)r. One full sequential update is Q=-(I+rL)^(-1)rU; its (i,j) entry is r[(1-r)^(i-j)1_{j<=i}-(1-r)^i]. Independent triangular solves for m=2,7,16,24 and c=.5,1,2,5 matched this exact matrix within 2e-14. Scaling mr->c, logarithm(1-r)=-c/m+O(1/m²) uniformly away from a total diagonal-cell area 1/m proves the O_c(m^-1/2) Hilbert–Schmidt limit. Exact Gram square roots yield physical similarity S_c=I+(sqrt(1+c)-1)P and the same rate in Schatten 2. Nonzero eigenfunctions of T_c solve df/ds=c(1-λ)f/λ, with boundary equation (z+c)e^z=c, z≠0; the principal Lambert root is excluded and all other branches are simple. Compact spectral approximation yields limiting spectral radius in (0,1); every fixed physical singular value converges. TV formula is c(m-1)/(m(m+c)). Bounds depend on c, which is fixed.
residual_risks: Non-normal finite matrices have no uniform spectral perturbation bound at zero; claimed result concerns isolated nonzero eigenvalues and spectral radius, for fixed c.
The explicit Lambert eigenvalues are not explicit singular values of the nonnormal limit.
